entry.title: Shentu v0.3.0
entry.content:
• Windows Server 2022 and 2025, verified on GitHub-hosted windows-2022/2025 runners (amd64; arm64 built too): a Windows collector reads the host through the Windows APIs only (registry, services, processes, sockets, accounts, scheduled tasks, the event log, WMI and the firewall), no PowerShell and no external commands.
  • Windows checks: autostart entries (Run keys, services, scheduled tasks, startup folders, WMI event subscriptions), RDP without NLA, SMB signing and SMBv1, insecure WinRM, firewall profiles, Defender state and exclusions, logon failures and cleared logs.
  • Missing Windows updates against Microsoft's monthly security releases (MSRC), with the CISA KEV list marking the exploited ones first.
  • IIS: web roots from applicationHost.config; the code audit reads ASP and ASP.NET pages and flags webshells and scripts in upload folders, UTF-16 pages included.
  • Two Windows services, Shentu (patrol) and ShentuBot (Telegram), installed with shentu service install [--bot] from %ProgramFiles%\Shentu; configuration and state in %ProgramData%\Shentu, open to SYSTEM and Administrators only.
  • The ssh_logins, processes, accounts_audit and log_search tools work on Windows (logon events, process list, local accounts, event logs).
  • Failed SSH logins are read from journald first: its ssh and sshd units are labelled by journald itself, so a local user cannot forge them. The text logs (auth.log, secure) are read when journald is missing, times out (60 s), or has no sshd entries; anyone on the host can write an sshd line to them with logger, so auth_events is then partial with the new reason unverified_source, and brute-force findings and patrol SSH alerts carry a note saying so. A journal that hides the system's entries from a non-root user is no longer reported as "no failed logins".
  • Amazon Linux 2 and 2023: package vulnerabilities come from Amazon's ALAS advisories (the repositories' updateinfo, checked against the sha256 in repomd.xml and cached), Amazon Linux 2's extras topics included. Amazon Linux 1, past its end of life, answers "cannot tell". Recorded on an Amazon Linux 2023 VM; Amazon Linux 2 is covered by tests only.
  • Alpine Linux: packages from the apk database (OSV), OpenRC services and runlevels, /etc/local.d, busybox crond (/etc/crontabs, /etc/periodic) and /etc/inittab as persistence, and sshd lines of busybox syslog's auth facilities, marked unverified. Recorded on an Alpine 3.22 VM, as root and as a user.
  • SUSE: openSUSE Leap and Tumbleweed, and SLES, SLED and SLES for SAP (one OSV ecosystem per SLE 15 module; the ones OSV does not carry are listed as not queried). Leap is tested with a synthetic fixture and SLES on no real host yet.
  • The daily report says when a vulnerability check failed or covered only part, and a package list that parsed to nothing is "cannot tell" instead of "no vulnerabilities".
  • macOS (new, read-only, never with sudo): platform, accounts (dscl), processes, listeners (netstat, or lsof when macOS hides sockets), the application firewall, SIP, Gatekeeper, FileVault, XProtect, launchd jobs and other persistence, sshd settings, and installed apps and Homebrew packages. The OS version is checked against Apple's software update catalog (gdmf.apple.com); packages answer "cannot tell", since OSV has no Homebrew ecosystem. Tested only with a synthetic fixture (an invented host); not yet verified on a real Mac. Login items are not parsed (the Background Task Management store), so macOS persistence is always partial. periodic.conf and daily/weekly/monthly.local are listed line by line, every line but blanks and plain comments (a # line with no quote, $ or backtick: in a heredoc such a line is data and runs its commands); they are short. A stock /etc/defaults/periodic.conf is left out, and the files periodic_conf_files names are read too.
  • A code audit root written with a trailing slash (/var/www/html/) or as / is no longer skipped when an audit resumes inside it. Roots are now cleaned, so the first audit after the upgrade does not find the place the last one stopped and walks from the start once.
  • sshd settings: a Match block inside an included file (Include sshd_config.d/*.conf) no longer hides the settings that follow the Include in the main file (sshd restores the Match state after each Include), so e.g. a later PermitRootLogin yes is reported. An Include nested more than 4 deep, or past 256 config files, is listed as unread.
  • Building from source now needs Go 1.26 or later (was 1.23): the Windows collector uses golang.org/x/sys, the second dependency.
  • Windows is read-only: block_ip and unblock_ip are not supported there.
  • Windows Server 2019 is best effort: expected to work (the same Windows APIs, build 17763) but not verified on GitHub-hosted runners (they offer no 2019 image).
  • shentu setup does not run on Windows yet; the configuration is written by hand.
  • The Windows binary is not code-signed and there is no MSI; SmartScreen or an antivirus may warn about it.

entry.title: Shentu v0.2.5
entry.content:
• app_code_audit follows calls across files: input read in one file and used in a sink of another is reported at the sink, with the file it came from.
  • Framework route models: the parameters of WordPress hooks, shortcodes and REST routes, Laravel routes, Django URLs, Flask and FastAPI views and Express handlers are input, also when the route is registered in another file.
  • New rule classes: LDAP injection, NoSQL operator injection, dangerous file uploads, weak cryptography and hard-coded credentials; TypeScript files are checked with the JavaScript rules.
  • Audits keep their results between runs, so a large application is covered over a few patrols instead of one.
  • The audit sizes itself to the server: heap at most min(1 GiB, 25% of available memory, 50% of the service's cgroup), workers from the CPU count and the load.
  • Fewer false positives: wp_send_json output, JSON_HEX_TAG data blocks, MongoDB queries on objects that are not collections, and Django _meta.get_field checks.
  • An audit spread over several runs can still report a few findings that differ from one run without a time limit; a fix is in progress.
  • php-deserialization-phar-wrapper reports filesize() on an upload's temporary path in WordPress's REST attachments controller, a false positive: the path is PHP's own, but the engine cannot yet tell an upload's tmp_name from its client-set name.
  • js-nosqli-mongo-query reports TypeORM repository calls on SQL databases (find/findOne whose options hold a where built from request values, e.g. n8n's public API and credential lookups) as MongoDB queries; TypeORM sends those values as SQL parameters, so these are false positives, to be told apart by a TypeORM-aware receiver check in v0.2.6.
  • js-cmdi-spawn-shell still reports spawn() and execFile() calls whose command and arguments are fixed when only the options (such as cwd or env) carry request values.
  • js-xss-response has no Server-Sent Events exception: res.write("data: " + value) in a text/event-stream handler is reported as XSS (a false positive), and nothing is missed because of SSE; telling streams apart by the handler's Content-Type is planned for v0.2.6.
  • ->get_settings() counts as Elementor widget input in every class, so WP_Widget::get_settings() and WooCommerce WC_Settings_Page::get_settings() values (saved by administrators) are reported too. Limiting the source to classes extending \Elementor\Widget_Base needs class-scoped sources in the engine (planned for v0.2.6). Values read through ->get_settings() can also be followed into WordPress admin field definitions and into a few SQL sinks that are already guarded (an isset() check, or a value bound through $wpdb->prepare() inside ORDER BY FIELD()), which gives extra false positives there. Narrowing the source to Elementor widgets is planned for v0.2.6.
  • In $wpdb->prepare()/->prepare() formats, a placeholder list built by a callback that returns a constant (implode(',', array_map(fn($v) => '%d', $ids)), or the same with function ($v) { return '%d'; }) is still treated as input and reported when $ids comes from the request. array_fill(0, count($ids), '%d') and sizeof() are recognised. Reading a callback's return value needs an engine change (planned for v0.2.6).
  • python-path-traversal-send-file reports zipfile.ZipFile(request.files[...]), which opens the uploaded stream rather than a path, a false positive. Telling a request's file stream from a client-set file name inside one argument needs an engine change (planned for v0.2.6).

Rules: 37 added, 0 removed.

entry.title: Shentu v0.2.4
entry.content:
• Rules move to their own format, checked in CI, starting with 33 rules.
  • accounts_audit reports shared SSH keys, ld.so.preload and PAM modules that belong to no package.
  • processes flags cryptominers.
  • Patrol reports one line per webshell.

Rules: 33 added, 0 removed.

entry.title: Shentu v0.2.1
entry.content:
• shentu bot: talk to Shentu from Telegram, with guarded pairing and four ranges of levels.
  • Usage tracking and an optional monthly AI budget.
  • Round 2 of the model comparison: 14 models, 11 scenarios.

entry.title: Shentu v0.2.0
entry.content:

  • Site survey and an application dependency scan.

entry.title: Shentu v0.1.1
entry.content:
• package_vulns marks actively exploited vulnerabilities (CISA KEV).
  • Slack and Discord webhooks.
  • Security invariant tests, a prompt-injection suite and govulncheck before each release.

entry.title: Shentu v0.1.0
entry.content: • First release: shentu chat and shentu patrol for Linux servers, with shentu setup for a local model or an API key.
